questions.stem: The slogan 'SWARAJ IS MY BIRTHRIGHT, AND I SHALL HAVE IT' was given by:
questions.explanation: BAL GANGADHAR TILAK (1856-1920) — ‘LOKMANYA' ('accepted by the people'); leader of the EXTREMIST / RADICAL faction of the Indian National Congress (INC) + icon of early militant nationalism. FAMOUS SLOGAN: 'SWARAJ IS MY BIRTHRIGHT AND I SHALL HAVE IT' — uttered during his 1908 sedition trial in Bombay HC. BOOKS: 'GITA RAHASYA' (written in Mandalay prison 1908-14 on Bhagavad Gita's karma yoga), 'The Arctic Home in the Vedas', 'The Orion'. NEWSPAPERS: KESARI (Marathi, 1881) + MAHRATTA (English) — sharp anti-British journalism. MASS MOBILISATION: revived GANAPATI FESTIVAL (1893) + SHIVAJI JAYANTI (1895) as public, anti-colonial mobilisation tools — making festivals community-wide instead of private. LAL-BAL-PAL TRIO: TILAK (Maharashtra) + Lala LAJPAT RAI (Punjab) + BIPIN CHANDRA PAL (Bengal) = Extremist trinity. Advocated boycott of British goods, Swadeshi, National Education. SURAT SPLIT (1907) — Congress split between MODERATES (Gokhale, Phirozeshah Mehta) + EXTREMISTS (Tilak, Lajpat, Pal) over the 'four resolutions' (Swadeshi, Boycott, National Education, Self-government). Reunited at LUCKNOW SESSION 1916 (also signed Lucknow Pact between INC + Muslim League). IMPRISONMENT: 1908-14 — 6 years in MANDALAY prison (Burma) for sedition (published articles critical of British). HOMERULE LEAGUE: founded 1916 with Annie Besant — demanded Home Rule for India within Empire (like Canada, Australia). DEATH: 1 August 1920 (same year Gandhi's Non-Cooperation Movement began). Called 'Father of Indian Unrest' by V.B. Fielding. leader of the Extremists + called 'LOKMANYA' ('accepted by the people').

questions.stem: The SURAT SPLIT of 1907 divided the Indian National Congress into:

options.option_text: MODERATES (Gokhale, Mehta, S.N. Banerjee) vs EXTREMISTS

questions.explanation: SURAT SPLIT (26 December 1907) — the famous rift at the Surat Congress Session over differences in METHODS + STRATEGY. MODERATES: Gopal Krishna Gokhale, Pherozeshah Mehta, Surendranath Banerjee, Dadabhai Naoroji, Dinshaw Wacha, R.C. Dutt — believed in constitutional agitation, petitions, prayers, cooperation with British, gradual reforms. EXTREMISTS: Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Lala Lajpat Rai, Bipin Chandra Pal ('Lal-Bal-Pal'), Aurobindo Ghosh — believed in direct action, boycott of British goods, passive resistance, Swadeshi, National Education, swaraj. IMMEDIATE CAUSE: (1) Moderates wanted to hold the session at Nagpur (Tilak's stronghold) — shifted to SURAT under pressure. (2) Moderates opposed Rash Behari Ghose (then Nagpur president-elect moderate) being nominated again. (3) Key 4 Surat resolutions on Swadeshi, Boycott, National Education, Self-Government were proposed by Extremists; Moderates wanted watered-down versions. CHAOS: scuffle in the pandal; Tilak thumped by a shoe (thrown at Surendranath Banerjee, hit Tilak); session suspended. RESULT: Extremists WALKED OUT + were EXPELLED from Congress. Congress remained moderate-led till 1916. CONGRESS REUNIFIED at LUCKNOW SESSION 1916 (after Tilak's return from Mandalay); this year also saw LUCKNOW PACT between Congress + Muslim League (Jinnah's famous negotiation). IMPACT: Surat split set back nationalist movement — until Gandhi's 1915 return from South Africa + 1917 emergence (Champaran). PARTITION OF BENGAL (1905, Curzon) was the spark that radicalised the movement + produced the Swadeshi + Boycott movement. REVOKED Partition in 1911 + shifted capital from Calcutta to Delhi. over methods + Swadeshi-boycott; Tilak, Lajpat Rai, Pal, Aurobindo.

questions.stem: The PARTITION OF BENGAL (1905) was carried out by Viceroy ______, ostensibly for administrative efficiency.
questions.explanation: PARTITION OF BENGAL — announced 19 July 1905, effective 16 OCTOBER 1905, by Viceroy LORD CURZON (Viceroy 1899-1905). DIVIDED Bengal Presidency into: (1) BENGAL (with Bihar + Orissa) — Hindu-majority, ~4.2 crore population; (2) EASTERN BENGAL + ASSAM — Muslim-majority, ~3.1 crore, new province with Dacca as capital. OFFICIAL REASON: administrative convenience (Bengal was too large + unwieldy). REAL REASON (widely condemned by Indian historians): DIVIDE + RULE — weaken the strong Bengali-led nationalist movement (Bengal was then the main centre of INC, Swadeshi, anti-British agitation) by splitting Hindus + Muslims. RESPONSE: MASS PROTESTS all over India. (1) 16 October 1905 = 'day of mourning' (rakhi-bandhan between Hindus + Muslims led by Tagore). (2) SWADESHI MOVEMENT — boycott of British goods, promotion of Indian-made (inaugurated 7 Aug 1905 at Calcutta Town Hall); burning of British textiles at Parel. (3) BOYCOTT of British institutions, courts, schools — NATIONAL EDUCATION movement (founding of Bengal National College; Aurobindo Ghosh's principalship). (4) SAMITIS (volunteer corps) formed. (5) Revolutionary violence rose (Anushilan Samiti, Jugantar, Muzaffarpur bombing 1908 by Khudiram Bose + Prafulla Chaki). TAGORE composed 'AMAR SONAR BANGLA' as protest anthem (later Bangladesh's national anthem). REVERSAL: British ANNULLED the partition in DECEMBER 1911 at Delhi Durbar (King George V), also shifting capital from CALCUTTA to DELHI the same year. But OUTCOMES persisted: (a) gave massive fillip to Swadeshi + nationalist movement; (b) birth of Muslim League 1906 (All India Muslim League in Dhaka — to safeguard Muslim interests during the Eastern Bengal province's popularity). Partition's communalising effect lingered + contributed to 1947 Partition. cited administrative convenience; real aim was to divide Hindu-majority + Muslim-majority areas + weaken Bengali nationalism.

questions.stem: AUROBINDO GHOSH, before his spiritual turn, was associated with which extremist revolutionary organisation?
questions.explanation: AUROBINDO GHOSH (1872-1950, later 'Sri Aurobindo') — pre-1910 EXTREMIST revolutionary; post-1910 spiritual PHILOSOPHER. EARLY LIFE: born Calcutta; educated in England (age 7-21) at ICSE + St. Paul's + King's College Cambridge (classics). Worked in Baroda State (1893-1906). NATIONALIST PHASE (1906-1910): returned to Bengal after Partition (1905); became editor of newspapers 'BANDE MATARAM' + 'KARMAYOGIN'; Principal of Bengal National College. Articulated 'spiritual nationalism' — India's freedom as divine mission. REVOLUTIONARY INVOLVEMENT: ANUSHILAN SAMITI founded 1902 by Promotha Nath Mitra; Aurobindo + his brother Barindra Kumar Ghosh were its key ideologues + organisers. JUGANTAR — the militant extremist wing of Anushilan — Barindra led it. MUZAFFARPUR BOMBING 1908 — KHUDIRAM BOSE (18) + PRAFULLA CHAKI threw a bomb at the carriage of Magistrate KINGSFORD (who gave harsh sentences to nationalists); killed Mrs + Miss KENNEDY (British ladies) instead. Khudiram was HANGED (11 Aug 1908, YOUNGEST martyr at 18); Chaki shot himself. ALIPORE CONSPIRACY CASE (1908-09) — Aurobindo ARRESTED + TRIED for sedition + conspiracy; 38 accused; defended by CHITTARANJAN DAS in a legendary year-long trial ending in Aurobindo's ACQUITTAL. SPIRITUAL TURN: while in jail, Aurobindo had mystical experiences reading the Gita; on release 1909, gradually withdrew from politics. 1910 — moved to PONDICHERRY (French India, safe from British) + devoted himself to integral yoga. AUROBINDO ASHRAM founded; along with THE MOTHER (Mirra Alfassa) in 1920s-30s developed INTEGRAL YOGA philosophy. Writings: 'The Life Divine', 'The Synthesis of Yoga', 'Savitri' (epic poem). AUROVILLE founded 1968 near Pondicherry by the Mother — international township experiment. Aurobindo's birthday 15 August coincided with India's Independence Day — auspicious symbolism. led ideologically by Aurobindo + his brother Barindra; involved in Muzaffarpur bombing + Alipore Conspiracy case (1908-09).

questions.stem: The KAKORI TRAIN ROBBERY (9 August 1925) was carried out by:

options.option_text: HRA — Hindustan Republican Association (later HSRA) — led by RAMPRASAD BISMIL, CHANDRA SHEKHAR AZAD, ASHFAQULLAH KHAN, ROSHAN SINGH, RAJENDRA LAHIRI + others

questions.explanation: KAKORI TRAIN ROBBERY / KAKORI CONSPIRACY — 9 August 1925, at KAKORI village (near Lucknow, UP). HRA (HINDUSTAN REPUBLICAN ASSOCIATION) — revolutionary organisation founded 1924 at Kanpur by Sachindra Nath Sanyal; aimed at armed overthrow of British rule + federal republic. EXECUTORS: RAM PRASAD BISMIL (leader, also poet — 'Sarfaroshi ki tamanna...' credited widely to him, actually by Bismil Azimabadi — Bismil adopted it as HRA anthem), ASHFAQULLAH KHAN (Muslim revolutionary, Bismil's best friend — symbol of Hindu-Muslim revolutionary unity), ROSHAN SINGH, RAJENDRA LAHIRI, CHANDRASHEKHAR AZAD (escaped), Banwari Lal, Sachindra Bakshi, Manmath Nath Gupta + others — totally 10 revolutionaries. OPERATION: stopped the 8-Down Saharanpur-Lucknow train at Kakori by pulling the alarm chain; looted a government treasury of ~₹8,000 (some sources ₹4,600) to fund arms purchases + activities; a passenger (AHMED ALI) was killed by accidental firing (only casualty). BRITISH CRACKDOWN: massive manhunt; 40+ arrested; KAKORI CONSPIRACY CASE lasted 18 months. OUTCOMES: (1) BISMIL, ASHFAQULLAH, ROSHAN SINGH, LAHIRI — HANGED in Dec 1927 (at Gorakhpur, Faizabad, Allahabad, Gonda jails respectively). (2) Sanyal + others — deportation to Andamans + long sentences. (3) CHANDRASHEKHAR AZAD EVADED arrest, reorganised HRA as HSRA (Hindustan Socialist Republican Association, 1928 at Ferozeshah Kotla Delhi — socialist added) along with BHAGAT SINGH, SUKHDEV, RAJGURU, BATUKESHWAR DUTT. AZAD died on 27 Feb 1931 at Alfred Park Allahabad (Chandrashekhar Azad Park today), shooting himself with last bullet to remain 'AZAD' (free) — aged 24. HSRA carried out assembly bombing (1929 Bhagat Singh-Batukeshwar Dutt), Saunders murder (1928).

questions.stem: BHAGAT SINGH, SUKHDEV + RAJGURU were HANGED on:
questions.explanation: BHAGAT SINGH (1907-1931) — SHAHEED-E-AZAM (Supreme Martyr); SUKHDEV THAPAR, SHIVARAM RAJGURU — HANGED together at LAHORE CENTRAL JAIL on 23 MARCH 1931 (evening, BEFORE scheduled 6 AM the next day — to avoid mass rioting). Ages at death: Bhagat 23, Sukhdev 23, Rajguru 22. 23 MARCH now observed as SHAHEED DIWAS (Martyrs' Day). CHARGES: LAHORE CONSPIRACY CASE — murder of Asst Superintendent of Police JOHN SAUNDERS (17 Dec 1928). BACKGROUND: (a) SIMON COMMISSION (1927, all-white, no Indian members) faced 'SIMON GO BACK' protests; (b) at LAHORE on 30 Oct 1928, LALA LAJPAT RAI was lathi-charged by Supt JAMES SCOTT, grievously injured; died 17 Nov 1928. (c) HSRA vowed vengeance. On 17 Dec 1928 outside Lahore Police HQ, Bhagat + Rajguru shot SAUNDERS (mistaken for Scott); Chandrashekhar Azad covered their escape. 8 APRIL 1929 — ASSEMBLY BOMB: Bhagat Singh + BATUKESHWAR DUTT threw 2 non-lethal BOMBS in Central Legislative Assembly (Delhi) + 'INQUILAB ZINDABAD!' slogan + leaflets ('to make the deaf hear'), protesting against the Public Safety Bill + Trade Disputes Bill. SURRENDERED voluntarily to be tried + use trial as propaganda platform. LAHORE CONSPIRACY TRIAL (May 1930 – Oct 1930): found guilty; sentenced to hang. HUNGER STRIKE in jail (116 days by Jatin Das, who died) — demanding political-prisoner status. GANDHI-IRWIN PACT (5 Mar 1931) — Congress didn't insist on commuting death sentences (controversial historical debate). Bhagat + 2 comrades were CREMATED at HUSSAINIWALA (Ferozepur bank of Sutlej, Pakistan border) by British before news spread. MOTHER Vidyavati, BROTHER Kulbir + Kultar; ROLE MODEL: Kartar Singh Sarabha (Ghadar martyr). WRITINGS: 'Why I Am an Atheist' (1931 prison essay). Bhagat Singh remains India's most popular revolutionary icon. for the Lahore Conspiracy case (Saunders murder Dec 1928); 23 March now SHAHEED DIWAS.

questions.stem: The GHADAR PARTY was founded in 1913 in:
questions.explanation: GHADAR PARTY / GHADR PARTY ('Revolt Party') — founded 1 November 1913 in SAN FRANCISCO, California, by Indian emigrants (predominantly PUNJABI SIKHS, also Hindus + some Muslims) working as farmers + labourers on the Pacific Coast (USA, Canada). PRESIDENT: SOHAN SINGH BHAKNA. SECRETARY + intellectual leader: LALA HAR DAYAL (Oxford-educated radical, anarchist influenced; later exiled, died 1939 in US). PUBLICATION: 'GHADAR' newspaper (multilingual — Urdu, Punjabi, Gujarati, Hindi) distributed among Indian expats globally. IDEOLOGY: armed revolution to overthrow British Raj; republican + secular; 'India for the Indians'. OPPORTUNITY: outbreak of WWI in AUG 1914 — Ghadar leaders saw Britain's distraction as chance to spark uprising. PLAN: thousands of Ghadarites returned to Punjab by sea (via Hong Kong, Singapore, Shanghai) aiming to incite mutiny in British Indian Army + general revolt. FAILURE: British intelligence infiltrated the movement; informant network caught plans; mass arrests on arrival. KOMAGATA MARU INCIDENT (1914) — Japanese ship chartered by Gurdit Singh carrying 376 Punjabi passengers (mostly Sikh) denied entry to Canada (Vancouver) on racist exclusion laws; forced back; on return to Budge Budge near Calcutta (Sep 1914), police fired on them — 19 killed. Radicalised many who joined Ghadar. LAHORE CONSPIRACY CASE (1915) — main Ghadar-linked trial; 42 hanged, 114 transported to Andamans; notables hanged: KARTAR SINGH SARABHA (age 19, Bhagat Singh's hero), VISHNU GANESH PINGLE. FIRST LAHORE CONSPIRACY CASE was this 1915 one (second was Bhagat Singh's 1929). LEGACY: (1) Inspired subsequent revolutionaries (Bhagat Singh held Sarabha's photo close to heart); (2) Canada's Komagata Maru apology (2016 by PM Trudeau); (3) Ghadar Memorial in San Francisco + Jalandhar (Deshbhagat Yadgar Hall). by Indian emigrants (Punjabi Sikhs + Hindus) led by LALA HAR DAYAL + Sohan Singh Bhakna; aimed at armed overthrow of British Raj via expat uprising.

questions.stem: The JALLIANWALA BAGH MASSACRE took place on:
questions.explanation: JALLIANWALA BAGH MASSACRE — 13 APRIL 1919 (BAISAKHI Day), at Jallianwala Bagh, AMRITSAR, Punjab. CONTEXT: (1) ROWLATT ACT (March 1919) — allowed arrest + indefinite detention without trial; opposed as 'no appeal, no plea, no dalil'; Gandhi called it 'Black Act' + launched ROWLATT SATYAGRAHA (his first nationwide movement, April 1919). (2) In Punjab, arrests of popular local leaders DR SATYAPAL + DR SAIFUDDIN KITCHLEW on 10 April 1919 triggered protests; police fired + killed 2-3, mob then killed 5 British in retaliation (Marcia Sherwood assault, bank employees killed). (3) Punjab Lt-Governor Michael O'Dwyer + General REGINALD DYER imposed martial law, banned gatherings. (4) 13 April, Baisakhi + annual Amritsar fair — ~20,000 people (many unaware of ban) gathered at Jallianwala Bagh (a walled enclosure with single narrow entrance) to peacefully protest + celebrate Baisakhi. (5) GENERAL DYER arrived with ~90 Gurkha + Baluchi soldiers + blocked the entrance; WITHOUT WARNING ordered 10 MINUTES of continuous rifle fire (1,650 rounds); pit ceased only when ammunition ran out. (6) Many jumped into the well to escape bullets (120 bodies retrieved from it, still preserved as memorial). DEATHS: Official British tally = 379 dead + 1,100 injured; Indian INC estimate = 1,000+ dead. AFTERMATH: (1) HUNTER COMMITTEE (1919-20) — inquiry: criticised Dyer for 'serious error of judgment' but didn't prosecute him; House of Lords supported him; British public raised £26,000 fund for 'The Saviour of Punjab'. (2) Rabindranath TAGORE RENOUNCED KNIGHTHOOD (31 May 1919). (3) Gandhi returned his Kaiser-i-Hind Medal; launched NON-COOPERATION MOVEMENT (1920-22). (4) UDHAM SINGH — Amritsar resident present at massacre, AVENGED the atrocity on 13 March 1940 by shooting Michael O'Dwyer at Caxton Hall, London; Udham Singh hanged 31 July 1940 at Pentonville Prison. (5) Dyer retired 1920; died 1927. British PM David Cameron (2013) + UK govt have repeatedly refused a formal apology (deepest 'regret' offered). General REGINALD DYER opened fire on a peaceful crowd; ~400-1000+ killed.

questions.stem: The INDIAN NATIONAL ARMY (INA / Azad Hind Fauj) was founded in 1942 in ______ by Captain Mohan Singh, later REVIVED + led by Subhas Chandra Bose.
questions.explanation: INDIAN NATIONAL ARMY (INA) / AZAD HIND FAUJ — formed to liberate India from British rule with Axis (Japanese) military support during WWII. PHASES: (1) FIRST INA (1942) — founded 17 FEBRUARY 1942 in SINGAPORE by Captain MOHAN SINGH (Indian Army officer captured by Japanese in Malaya); initial strength ~40,000 from Indian POWs surrendered after Japan's lightning victories in Malaya + Singapore. RASH BEHARI BOSE (earlier revolutionary, fled to Japan in 1915) — gave political leadership. First INA disbanded Dec 1942 due to Japanese-INA disputes (Japanese treated INA as subordinate); Mohan Singh arrested by Japanese. (2) SECOND INA (1943) — SUBHAS CHANDRA BOSE reached Japan via dramatic escape: (a) Jan 1941 — escaped house arrest in Calcutta, via Afghanistan to Berlin; (b) Met Hitler (May 1942) — coined title 'NETAJI' (Leader), received by Indian soldiers as Indische Legion; (c) Feb 1943 — submarine voyage from Kiel to Madagascar to Japanese submarine, to Tokyo (July 1943); (d) 4 July 1943 in SINGAPORE — Bose took command of INA. (e) 21 OCTOBER 1943 — Declared AZAD HIND GOVERNMENT (Provisional Government of Free India) in Singapore; Bose was 'Head of State + Prime Minister + Minister of War'. Recognised by 9 Axis + neutral countries (Japan, Germany, Italy, Burma, Thailand, Nanking China, Manchukuo, Philippines, Croatia). (f) Women's regiment — RANI OF JHANSI REGIMENT, led by CAPTAIN LAKSHMI SAHGAL (first all-women combat unit in modern Asia). (g) Slogans: 'Dilli Chalo!', 'Jai Hind!', 'Tum mujhe khoon do, main tumhe azadi dunga'. (h) Battles: INA's Bahadur brigade fought alongside Japanese in IMPHAL-KOHIMA OFFENSIVE (Mar-Jul 1944) — failed due to monsoon + Allied resistance; Japanese defeat; INA lost ~50% to disease, starvation, fighting. (i) NETAJI's DEATH: officially in air crash at TAIHOKU (Taipei), TAIWAN, 18 AUGUST 1945 — some dispute it, multiple commissions; Shah Nawaz (1956), Khosla (1974), Mukherjee (2005) differ. (3) POST-WAR: RED FORT TRIALS (Nov 1945 – Jan 1946) of 3 INA officers — PK Sahgal (Hindu), Shah Nawaz Khan (Muslim), Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon (Sikh) — symbolic communal unity; defended by Bhulabhai Desai, Asaf Ali, Nehru, Tej Bahadur Sapru; massive public sympathy + demos + Naval Mutiny (Feb 1946) forced British to commute sentences + speeded up Independence. initially formed in 1942 from Indian POWs of the Japanese; REVIVED + inspired by Subhas Bose in July 1943.

questions.stem: Which revolutionary is known for the slogan 'INQUILAB ZINDABAD' + its assembly-bombing association?
questions.explanation: 'INQUILAB ZINDABAD' (Urdu/Hindi: 'Long Live Revolution') — slogan popularised by BHAGAT SINGH + BATUKESHWAR DUTT during the CENTRAL LEGISLATIVE ASSEMBLY BOMBING (8 April 1929). ORIGIN of slogan: first used by poet MAULANA HASRAT MOHANI (a Muslim League Communist freedom fighter, from Mohan, UP — also coined 'Complete Independence' for INC + championed it at the 1921 Ahmedabad Session before Nehru formalised it at Lahore 1929). EVENT: on 8 April 1929 at Central Legislative Assembly (then in New Delhi, now Parliament complex), Bhagat Singh + Batukeshwar Dutt tossed TWO non-lethal bombs + red pamphlets from the visitors' gallery as the Assembly was debating the PUBLIC SAFETY BILL + TRADE DISPUTES BILL (oppressive measures). PURPOSE: (a) political theatre — not to kill (deliberately low-explosive bombs; no injuries reported); (b) 'TO MAKE THE DEAF HEAR' — to wake up the government + public to oppression; (c) use the trial as a propaganda platform. They SURRENDERED ON THE SPOT instead of escaping, shouting 'Inquilab Zindabad!' + 'Samrajyavaad ka nash ho!' ('Down with imperialism!'). TRIAL 1929-30: Bhagat was simultaneously linked via fingerprints to the earlier SAUNDERS murder (Dec 1928); LAHORE CONSPIRACY CASE added. Defended trial as political. Wrote extensively from jail — 'Why I Am an Atheist' (1931), manifestos for HSRA's socialist republic. EXECUTION 23 March 1931 alongside Sukhdev + Rajguru. BATUKESHWAR DUTT survived — sentenced to life in Andamans; released 1938; continued struggle; died 1965 in poverty (ironic — forgotten by govt till late). INQUILAB ZINDABAD became THE defining slogan of Indian revolutionary movement + continues to resonate in progressive politics across South Asia. on 8 April 1929 threw non-lethal bombs in the Central Legislative Assembly (Delhi) shouting 'Inquilab Zindabad!'.
